title: Design System: JBDC — The Atelier Ledger

title.purpose: Screen titles and a design's name — the moments the ledger names something.

label.purpose: Field labels, button text, stage names, materials.

mono.purpose: Ids, measurements, constants — data, not prose.

shadows.name: whisper
shadows.purpose: Resting cards, buttons, inputs — barely there.

shadows.name: dialog
shadows.purpose: The centered dialog, the deepest point in the system.

motion.name: overlay-enter
motion.purpose: Overlays and dialogs arriving; honors Reduce Motion.

motion.name: press
motion.purpose: Tonal shift to 90% (buttons) or opacity dip to 70% (cards).

narrative.overview:
JBDC is one designer's private catalog of her own clothing designs, and the interface reads as her bound studio notebook: warm paper surfaces, a wood-toned accent for the things that matter, serif titles like specimen labels. The photography is the artwork; the chrome is the furniture around it. The feel is warm, unhurried, precise — a working archive, not a showcase.

The system is quiet archival. Depth comes from paper tonal steps and hairline borders, never from shadow play; press feedback is a tonal shift, not a bounce; motion is a short fade that honors the system Reduce Motion setting. Color is spent on meaning only: Sanded Wood marks confirmed work and primary actions, Muslin Sage marks work in progress and active selection, Rejection Red marks what did not proceed. Everything else is paper and ink.
keyCharacteristics: Paper tonal hierarchy — Warm Paper page, Unbleached Paper cards, Kraft Layer insets — instead of shadows
Cormorant Garamond titles over DM Sans body; DM Mono for ids, measurements, constants
Two accents with fixed meanings: Sanded Wood (confirmed/primary), Muslin Sage (in-progress/active); red is rejection only
Hairline Thread Line borders everywhere; dashed borders are the signature for empty attach points
Photography leads at fixed ratios: 4:5 hero, 3:4 thumbs, square compact covers
Fades ≤ 200ms, honoring Reduce Motion; nothing bounces or loops

rules.name: The Ink-and-Paper Rule
rules.body: Color is state, not decoration. Wood = confirmed and primary, Sage = in-progress and active, Red = rejection and destruction. No third accent hue ever enters the system; everything else is paper and ink.

rules.name: The Overlay Exception
rules.body: Over photography only, chips may use translucent black (rgba(0,0,0,0.6)) with white text. Nowhere else does true black appear in the paper world.

rules.name: The Two Voices Rule
rules.body: Cormorant speaks only for titles — the names of screens, designs, and dialogs. Anything the Owner reads as information is DM Sans; anything read as data is DM Mono. Cormorant body text is forbidden.

rules.name: The Flat-Archive Rule
rules.body: A surface's importance is read from its tone, never from its shadow. If a shadow exists at all it stays ≤ 5% black; glass effects, large blurs, and decorative drop shadows do not enter this system.

rules.name: The Pill Rule
rules.body: Pills are for state and selection — badges, stage chips, toggles. Rectangles are for containers and controls. A pill never carries a sentence; a rectangle never carries a status.

rules.name: The Quiet Turn Rule
rules.body: Motion never announces — it only arrives and leaves, in 200ms or less. Every animation honors the system Reduce Motion setting with a crossfade or an instant cut.

dos: Do resolve every color through the slot table in Colors — wood is primary, sage is secondary, Kraft is muted/accent.
Do separate with Thread Line hairlines and group with Kraft Layer insets; let tone carry the hierarchy.
Do mark every empty attach point with the dashed frame — an empty stage, a missing cover, an add action.
Do keep Cormorant for titles only, DM Sans for information, DM Mono for ids and measurements.
Do use fades of 200ms or less that honor the system Reduce Motion setting.
Do lay out inside safe-area insets and end every scroll in 48px of breathing room.
Do write empty and error states plainly, in sentence case, with one action — and name terminology from GLOSSARY.md.
donts: Don't introduce any accent hue beyond wood, sage, and red.
Don't lift a card with a shadow heavier than the 5% whisper; no glass, no gradients, no blur backdrops.
Don't set a status in anything but a pill — never a rectangle, a banner, or a colored row.
Don't fill an empty stage with illustration or icon decoration; the dashed frame is the empty state.
Don't announce a save with a toast or a banner; History is a screen the Owner opens.
Don't animate an entrance longer than 200ms, or with a spring that bounces.
Don't use true black or pure white inside the paper world; the only blacks live over photography.
